correctness.rationale: For H as a chosen root edge set, the only undominated root edges are the complete bipartite graph on unused roots and the isolated chosen edges. The potential |U|-i gains 1 or 2 per legal choice and gains 2 at the first nontrivial component, yielding at most m+n-1. An equality sequence can exhaust the final unused root only at that unique gain-2 step, proving |m-n|=1 and forcing an ordered saturated matching plus successive attachments. Explicit sequences prove both lower bounds. Multiplication of labeled matching, spare-vertex and attachment choices gives the stated factorial count. The standalone verifier exhaustively checks all listed boards, including every optimal sequence on 2x3 and 3x4.

value.rationale: The general graph-product Grundy total-domination literature motivates determining exact worst-case lengths. The rook-graph case has a sharp nonmonotone one-step aspect-ratio anomaly not seen from the elementary star construction, and the exhaustive matching/attachment classification gives a factorial number of ordered optimal greedy histories. The precise factor-difference exception and exact optimizer enumerator are structurally meaningful and may inform skew zero forcing via the known correspondence.
